key_insight: A tin-vacancy (SnV) center in diamond can emit highly indistinguishable single photons, with intrinsic performance approaching perfection for quantum-network use.
engineering_relevance: This makes SnV centers a strong candidate for repeater-based quantum communication and photonic quantum information processing, including long-distance telecom links.
method: Coherently excite an SnV spin qubit in diamond to generate single photons.
Measure Hong-Ou-Mandel two-photon interference to quantify indistinguishability.
Apply quantum frequency conversion to the telecom C-band and assess network performance with Monte Carlo repeater simulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports raw Hong-Ou-Mandel visibilities above 0.95, intrinsic indistinguishability up to 0.999, and preserved performance after telecom conversion.
watch_item: The remaining gap to ideal performance is mainly technical rather than fundamental, so system integration, source stability, and conversion losses will still matter in practice.
paper_title: Highly indistinguishable photons from a tin-vacancy spin qubit in diamond
